sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house fast in Lubbock?
sections.html:
Three paths are open in Lubbock: hire a listing agent, handle the sale on your own, or let a cash buyer take the house in its current state. Each route trades time, price and effort differently, and the right one depends on the condition of the house, any liens on it and how soon you need the money.

The seat of Lubbock County and the biggest city on the South Plains, on Interstate 27 about 327 miles northwest of Dallas and 122 miles south of Amarillo, at an elevation of 3,256 feet. That setting shapes the housing market. The city is a regional hub for health care, higher education and agriculture, so houses tend to sell to people tied to those employers, and a house in need of repair still has a pool of possible buyers.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, though showings, repair requests and lender timelines stretch the calendar.
  • Owner sale: skips the commission and puts pricing and paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: quick close, no repairs, typically priced under a polished retail sale.

sections.h2: What is Lubbock like as a place to own a house?
sections.html:
Lubbock is a flat High Plains city built around Texas Tech University, a medical center and a farm economy. The Texas State Historical Association records that the city was founded in 1890 when two rival settlements, Old Lubbock and Monterey, merged, and that it was incorporated as a city on March 16, 1909.

The Santa Fe railroad reached Lubbock in 1909, and in 1923 the legislature set up Texas Technological College there. The school became Texas Tech University in 1969, and a medical school followed in 1970 and grew into the Health Sciences Center. The same account counts seven hospitals with more than 2,000 beds, which makes health care a steady source of local housing demand.

Agriculture still matters. The surrounding country moved toward cotton and sorghum as irrigation spread in the 1930s, and Lubbock became the wholesale center for dozens of West Texas and eastern New Mexico counties. Reese Air Force Base closed in 1997 and was later redeveloped as the Reese Technology Center.

Weather is part of the story too. On May 11, 1970, a tornado devastated the city center and killed twenty-six people. Roofs, hail damage and storm shelters are fair questions for any Lubbock buyer, so a seller with an older roof should expect them in an inspection.

sections.h2: How does Lubbock's property tax system affect a seller?
sections.html:
Property in Lubbock is valued by the Lubbock Central Appraisal District, and taxes on it are billed once a year. Texas has no state property tax, so what you owe is set by local taxing units that tax your address, and the county or school district sets its own rate.

The district's website says the 2026 tax statements were mailed on October 23, 2026. It also noted that bills for properties in Lubbock Cooper ISD would wait until after a November 3, 2026 voter-approval tax rate election was decided. If you own in that school district, ask the district office which rate applies to your bill.

Statewide, the lien for a year's taxes attaches on January 1, and the delinquency date generally falls on February 1 when the bill is unpaid. Penalty and interest begin at that point and keep growing. At closing, a title company normally prorates the current year's tax between seller and buyer, so ask for the proration line on your settlement statement.

A warning on the district's own home page is worth repeating. Companies sometimes offer to file a homestead exemption for a one-time processing fee, and the district states there is never a fee to file for any exemption.

sections.h2: What does the Lubbock appraisal district offer homeowners?
sections.html:
Lubbock homeowners can file residence homestead exemptions online through the appraisal district's property search. The district lists the general residence homestead exemption plus those for disabled persons, owners 65 or older, 100 percent disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.

  • Every Texas school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and seniors or disabled owners get a further $60,000 off the school levy base.
  • The residence homestead appraisal cap limits yearly growth in appraised value to 10 percent, starting the year after the exemption is first granted.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may defer taxes on the homestead while they own and live in it. The deferred tax, penalty and interest come due 181 days after the property stops qualifying.

The district's number for questions is 806-762-5000. If you are selling, the exemption does not follow you, so a buyer who moves in after January 1 should file for their own.

sections.h2: How can I pay or check taxes on a Lubbock house?
sections.html:
You can look up an account on the appraisal district site, mail a check to P.O. Box 10568, Lubbock, TX 79408, use the drop box at 2109 Avenue Q, or pay by phone or online. The district says payment processing fees are charged by Certified Payments and not by the district.

Online and phone payment fees listed by the Lubbock Central Appraisal District
Payment methodFee as printed
Electronic checkFlat fee of $1.50

Debit card1% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00

Ask the district for a tax certificate if the title company requires one. Delinquent accounts can end up in a tax foreclosure sale, and the district's page describes a form 50-307 written statement request for those sales, which must be notarized and carries a $10.00 fee paid in certified funds.

sections.h2: What happens if I am behind on taxes or the mortgage in Lubbock?
sections.html:
Late payments on a Lubbock house leave a narrow window. A lender must give a default notice with twenty days to catch up, and an auction notice follows with three weeks of warning. Auctions run monthly, in a morning-to-afternoon window, at a spot the county sets.

Back property taxes work differently. A collector may offer a payment plan stretching up to 36 months on a homestead, and penalty relief is possible if you pay quickly and ask in writing. The Lubbock district's home page also describes a notarized written-statement request, with a $10.00 certified-funds fee, tied to tax foreclosure sales.

  • Selling ahead of the auction protects equity and keeps a foreclosure off your record.
  • Ask the lender for a payoff figure, and about a short sale if the balance tops value.
  • Search county records for liens so nothing surprises the title company.

sections.h2: How do inherited or tenant-occupied houses in Lubbock sell?
sections.html:
Both situations can end in a quick sale once paperwork is sorted. For an inherited Lubbock house, a will may be probated up to four years after death, and a muniment of title can let the will and court order stand in for a full administration. With no will, a small estate affidavit covers modest estates, and an affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that a buyer is free to refuse.

A rented house raises other timing questions. Written notice to leave is normally three days, a justice court hears the case, and a writ of possession is available six days after judgment. Cash buyers often accept a tenant in place, which avoids that sequence.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in Lubbock County?
sections.html: Your deed goes into the official records at the Lubbock County Clerk's office, after a notary or similar officer acknowledges the signature. State clerk guidance puts the base charge at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after. Confirm the current total with the clerk, though the closing agent usually files and pays from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lubbock house if it needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so a worn roof or old plumbing does not have to be fixed first. Expect the offer to reflect the repair cost, and compare it with an agent listing before you decide.

faqs.q: When are Lubbock property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: Texas treats most taxes as delinquent on February 1 if unpaid, with penalty and interest starting then. The Lubbock Central Appraisal District lists current statement dates on its website, and its office at 806-762-5000 can confirm your account.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to file a homestead exemption in Lubbock?
faqs.a: No. The appraisal district states there is never a fee to file for any exemption and warns owners not to respond to companies that ask for a one-time processing fee.

faqs.q: Does a Lubbock tax lien block a sale?
faqs.a: It complicates one. The lien for a year's tax attaches on January 1, and buyers cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid. A title company can pay them from your closing proceeds.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when I sell in Lubbock?
faqs.a: The Lubbock County Clerk records it, usually submitted by the title company. The instrument must be signed and acknowledged before a notary, and the clerk charges per-page recording fees.
